projects.title: Orb[i]s
projects.subtitle: The Future Culture
description: Orb[i]s a groundbreaking Design Research project by Roshni Gera, Elisavet Konstantinidou, Misbah Shehreen Baig and Yunzhu Duan from the Architecture and Urbanism (Design Research Laboratory) - from Spyropoulos studio, at Architectural Association School of Architecture, London.The project reimagines the future of urban environments through adaptive spatial infrastructure. The system transcends traditional architectural boundaries by introducing a Prototypical System composed of intelligent, self-assembling units capable of dynamic reconfiguration in response to urban needs and changes. These spheroidal units, equipped with telescopic legs and electromagnets, interact and rearrange themselves into various urban elements, demonstrating collective intelligence and flexibility. Beyond mere physical structures, Orb[i]s integrates advanced sensory systems and machine learning to enhance user interaction and adaptability, offering a visionary approach to urban development that champions adaptability, responsiveness and the seamless integration of technology and architecture to foster new forms of cultural and urban spaces.
Location : London, United Kingdom

projects.title: Vaults of Sechseläutenplatz
projects.subtitle: RhinoVault experiments to achieve Structural Elegance
description: A design proposal that utilises the unreinforced masonry of compression only structures, proposing a central vaulted attraction set in the heart of Zürich's Sechseläutenplatz town square. Through extensive experiments and iterations, Rhinovault was used to rationalise the architectural form, showcasing a harmonious balance of horizontal equilibriums. This innovative design not only enhances the square's aesthetic appeal but also introduces a self-supporting and stable structure, seamlessly integrating with the urban fabric of Zürich. Explore the intersection of functionality and beauty through the study of Vaults, paving the way for a visionary approach to contemporary architecture.
Location : Zurich, Switzerland

projects.title: Take a Seat
projects.subtitle: Recyclable Urban Furniture
description: The tiniest and only installation to be built on Church Street, as part of Bangalore’s Clean Air Street Movement. A temporary, yet Sustainable seater was made entirely out of 100% Recycled Paper Tubes (usually found as a refuse at Print stores). The installation was built to provoke the idea of Reduce- Reuse-Recycle and stood true to this idea by minimising the amount of waste generated even in the process of fabrication. All the segments of the seater were efficiently designed to make optimal use of the limited material available. The temporary yet sustainable Installation was used by several artists for their performances.The seater endured 1000’s of users and uses whilst serving a different function/experience to each one.

projects.title: An Outdoor Swing
projects.subtitle: Using perceived ‘waste’ as a resource
description: The outdoor swing utilised WoW Boards by Trashcon - a startup pioneering a sustainable approach by transforming non-biodegradable materials into building alternatives. By harnessing this innovative material, the outdoor swing design not only ensures durability but also boasts a playful mosaic-like appearance. This project showcases the potential to eliminate wood usage in various products while simultaneously addressing environmental concerns.

projects.title: Custom Shoe Stands
description: Designed for a school where children leave their shoes outside classrooms, these custom-crafted stands transform a functional necessity into a design feature. Made from Relwood, an engineered material that is strong, weather-resistant, and versatile to thermoform or laser cut, the stands balance durability with refined aesthetics.Inspired by global sneaker culture, the design maximizes storage while occupying minimal floor space, keeping lobbies clutter-free and visually engaging. More than just racks, these shoe stands add character to the space while supporting daily routines with efficiency and ease.
School name : Head Start Educational Academy, Bangalore
Design Team : Stavya Architects and RGB design
Material and manufacture : Merlecha Corporation
Location : Bangalore, India
Photography : Vaishali Bhatia

projects.title: Library at Head Start Educational Academy
projects.subtitle: A space where curves guide curiosity
description: The library at Head Start Academy was designed as a place where imagination flows as freely as its forms. Guided by curvilinear lines and crafted details, the space integrates bookshelves, seating and work areas into a seamless environment that feels bright, open and inviting.At its heart sits the custom Sinuo Table, a versatile piece that supports solo reading, group discussions and quick browsing with its integrated storage, while curved shelves and cozy nooks encourage children to settle in with their favourite books. Every element from textures and finishes to lighting and layout was designed with intention, balancing functionality with playfulness.The result is a library that is both practical and poetic, a space where design quietly supports creativity, learning and collaboration.
Craftsmanship & Execution - Bram Woodcrafting Studio, Mysore
Photography and Videography - Anand Jaju
Location - Bangalore, India

projects.title: Circle Packing
projects.subtitle: Shoe storage that encourages interaction and play
description: Circle Packing is a thoughtfully designed shoe storage solution that encourgaes social interaction among students while making efficient use of space. Constructed from durable PVC pipes, the design introduces playful pops of color against the school’s warm, earthy brick tones, combining functionality with visual vibrancy. A custom detail was designed to embed and conceal all supporting framework, ensuring a clean, seamless appearance. PVC was chosen not only for its flexibility in design but also for its durability and resistance to wear and also allowing frequent washability when compared to conventional materials.Arranged into flexible, modular units, the system allows for easy rearrangement as needed, supporting both organization and adaptability.
School name : Head Start Educational Academy, Bangalore
Design team : Stavya Architects and RGB Design
Location : Bangalore, India
Photograpy : Vaishali Bhatia

projects.title: TETR.IS
projects.subtitle: Recyclable Installation for Dubai Design Week 2023
description: TETR.IS revolutionises sustainable design by transforming non-recycled aseptic packaging into a captivating installation for Dubai Design Week Urban Commissions 2023. Eschewing traditional adhesives, this innovative process separates tetra pack components, recycling them into durable, aesthetic sheets for construction, without generating waste. Inspired by the game 'tetris', TETR.IS's modular form visually represents the challenge of tetra pack waste, embodying a zero-waste, closed-loop lifecycle. This project not only highlights environmental sustainability but also redefines material reuse, setting a new standard for eco-friendly design.
Material wizard : Material Library of India, Noida
Project for : Dubai Design Week, 2023
Location: Dubai, UAE

projects.title: Susegad Cube  - Serendipity Arts Festival 2024
projects.subtitle: Building stillness, space and play
description: The Susegad Cube, part of the Panjim Cube project, is an immersive installation designed to evoke calm, curiosity and the leisurely essence of Goan life. The Cube explores complex geometry with high structural efficiency and spatial intrigue. Its intersecting channels, meeting at precise angles, divide space into organic cocoons, offering visitors personal nooks to pause, play and engage.Every aspect of the Cube, from sketches to simulation, fabrication and final installation, was guided by experimentation, cultural context and a commitment to minimal material waste. The modular design allowed efficient assembly, seamless transport, and installation - fabricated, painted and finished in Bangalore before travelling 900 km to Panjim for the festival.At the Serendipity Arts Festival, the Susegad Cube became a vibrant yet serene space where Panjim’s culture meets interactive design. Visitors could explore, relax and define their own sense of contentment, experiencing stillness in a structure that is as playful as it is contemplative. The installation celebrates the balance between geometry, craftsmanship and the human desire for quiet moments, transforming the Cube into both a visual and experiential ode to Susegad, the art of slow living.
Design Team : Dasein Lab and RGB Design
For : Serendipity Art Festival 2024
Curators : Thukral and Tagra
Location : Panjim, Goa
Photography, Drone Videography : Vaishali Bhatia

projects.title: Conference Room
description: The HSEA Conference Room Renovation project revitalized a 12-year-old space, prioritizing functionality, aesthetics, and virtual meeting capabilities. A standout feature is the custom-fabricated central false ceiling, meticulously designed to optimize weight of the structure whilst being coherence with the wall panels, adding a focal point and enhancing the overall ambiance of the space for meetings and collaboration.
Project done in collaboration with Stavya Architects
School name : Head Start Educational Academy, Bangalore
Location : Bangalore, India
Photography : Anand Jaju

projects.title: Dining Hall
projects.subtitle: A space where meals become a ritual of care, culture and community
description: Spanning 2,500 sqft., the dining hall at Head Start Educational Academy was reimagined to serve more than food, it serves values. Every day, 250-300 middle school students move through the space with ease: walking in lines, serving themselves, sitting on the floor with teachers, eating mindfully, washing their plates and leaving behind zero food waste.The design of the space quietly supports this daily rhythm. Sound reverberation was reduced by introducing a mildly textured flooring, while neutral white panel lights make the hall brighter and more grounded, playfulness is brought in through terrazzo counters, whose curves and forms were directly informed by mapping student movement patterns. To ensure efficiency, the wet area was cordoned off with a different colour and texture, clearly separating wet and dry zones. Together, these interventions absorb sound, guide flow, and spark interaction, transforming lunchtime into a shared ritual of responsibility, equality and mindfulness.
Design Team : Stavya Architects and RGB design
Photography and Videography : Anand Jaju
Location : Bangalore, India

projects.title: Prestige Oakwood Kitchen
projects.subtitle: Minimalist Kitchen with a Contemporary-Classical Twist
description: A kitchen that embodies calm, clarity and quiet elegance. Designed with a white and beige palette, this space balances minimalist lines with a subtle contemporary-classical twist, creating a timeless setting that feels both refined and welcoming.Impeccable finishes, warm lighting and carefully chosen materials come together to form a kitchen that is as functional as it is beautiful. Every surface and detail was crafted to reflect the client’s vision of simplicity without sterility - minimal, yet full of character.
Execution partner : Casantro
Photography : Casantro
Location : Bangalore, India

projects.title: Flames of Growth & Glory
projects.subtitle: Notions of India - Design entry
description: The design of the installation encapsulates the cultural mosaic of India through a geometric rangoli-inspired base and ascending steel curves, symbolising the nation's robust diversity and continual ascent. Alternating panels of corten steel reflect the rich tapestry of Indian heritage, while open spaces invite periodic cultural expressions, embodying India's adaptability. Culminating in flames that represent the eternal spirit of hope and resilience, this sculpture is a timeless tribute to India's shared history and democratic ethos, a beacon of unity and progress.

projects.title: SEA Pavilion
description: The SEA Pavilion explores Mumbai's urban contrasts, where vibrant informal settlements coexist alongside towering skyscrapers, revealing both resilience and inequality. The design addresses environmental challenges through an adaptive tarpaulin roof that responds to rain, humidity, and sunlight, and amphibious retrofits that enhance flood resilience for vulnerable communities.The Speaking Walls illustrate rising sea levels, with household items at the base and solid upper sections representing water encroachment, eventually overtaken by vegetation -showcasing nature’s balance. The pavilion merges urban narrative, climate adaptation and interactive design into an immersive experience of Mumbai's evolving landscape.
Design Team : Krantinaari, Dasein Lab, RGB Design
Location : Mumbai, India
